method_card.title: Transforming Graphs with Function Notation
method_card.content: Graph transformations use function notation \(f(x)\). Changes outside the bracket affect \(y\) and behave as written: \(f(x) + a\) shifts up by \(a\), \(-f(x)\) reflects in the \(x\)-axis, and \(af(x)\) stretches vertically by scale factor \(a\). Changes inside the bracket affect \(x\) and do the opposite: \(f(x + a)\) shifts left by \(a\), \(f(-x)\) reflects in the \(y\)-axis, and \(f(ax)\) compresses horizontally by scale factor \(\frac{1}{a}\). In short: outside affects \(y\) as expected, inside affects \(x\) inversely.
method_card.example:
The point (3, 5) lies on \(y = f(x)\). Find its image on \(y = f(x + 2)\).

The \(+2\) is inside the bracket, so it moves the point LEFT by 2: \(x = 3 - 2 = 1\). The \(y\)-coordinate is unchanged, so the image is \((1, 5)\).

steps: A stretch changes the size of the curve: af(x) multiplies every y by a (vertical stretch, factor a).
f(ax) divides every x by a (horizontal stretch, factor 1/a), because inside affects x inversely.
To describe a transformation, name the type (translation, reflection or stretch) with its size and direction.

steps: Outside the bracket changes y: f(x) + a adds a to the y-coordinate, f(x) − a subtracts a.
Inside the bracket changes x and does the opposite: f(x + a) moves left (subtract from x), f(x − a) moves right (add to x).
Leave the coordinate that is not affected exactly as it was.
